problems: The WebFetch of Regency_of_Algiers is truncated inside the 1710 sentence; 1710-1830 had to be built from the Oran, Invasion of Algiers in 1830 and French conquest of Algeria pages.

Regency of Algiers starts 1706 in the dossier (Cliopatria's row) although the page dates it from 1516; its 1516-1705 land (793 Algerian cells 1560-1705) is inside the Cliopatria Ottoman Empire row. Likewise the Ottoman Empire row holds 544 Libyan cells and a 30-cell Tunisian strip to 1712 and 87 Tripolitanian cells in 1836-1839, which the Karamanli (1711-1712) and ottoman-tripolitania (1835-1839) dossiers now claim; the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) must drop them and should record the Regency of Algiers, Tripolitania and Tunis as de jure vassals.

Cliopatria's 'Regency of Algiers' shapes of 1830-1845 are the unconquered remainder of Algeria, not the Regency (which fell 5 July 1830): four are marked wrong and reassigned to emirate-of-abdelkader; the Constantinois, Kabylia and the Saharan oases have no owner. French Algeria's 1846 shape (211,876 km2) covers the whole country, which the emirate dossier records as a confidence-1 loss in 1846.

Cliopatria's Ottoman Tripolitania 1840-1884 shapes contain a stray 47-cell patch in Somaliland (and 11 cells on the Tunisian, Niger and Chad edges); marked adjust. khedivate-of-egypt (me-10) should check whether the patch is the Red Sea coast.

ottoman-tripolitania ends 18 October 1912 (Treaty of Ouchy) with a new 1912 keyframe, one year after Cliopatria's row; Italian Africa's Cliopatria 1912 shape covers Libya, so 1912 is a contest blend; the italian-africa dossier should mirror the contest from October 1911 and the gain in October 1912.

Counterpart strings used with no dossier yet: beylik-of-constantine (identity successors and a war only), 'Fezzan (Awlad Muhammad dynasty)' (vassal and gain events). The Tunis dossier's 1794 gain from karamanli-dynasty (confidence 1) matches the Karamanli loss.
Page budget: Algiers 5 pages, Karamanli 5, Tripolitania 5; the two extra dossiers used 4 and 1 (three of the Emirate's pages shared with Algiers). No curl/Wikidata/archive access was needed.
